claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I'm asking about my son Alex, he's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's helpful. Let me ask you a couple more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upbringing? For example, do you provide for his daily needs like food, clothes, and other essentials?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him - I provide all his food, clothes, and everything he needs day to day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, in care, or living away from home for any reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he was in care for a little while recently, but he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this situation a bit better:

**How long was Alex in care, and how long has he been back home with you now?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He was in care for about 8 weeks, and he's been back home with me now for a few weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**While Alex was in care during those 8 weeks, was the local council paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if the council was paying for his care during that time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's the situation:**

You meet many of the basic requirements:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex lives with you and you're responsible for his care ✓
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him ✓

**However**, there's a complicating factor: Alex was in care for approximately 8 weeks, and you're unsure whether the local council was paying towards his accommodation or maintenance during that time.

This information is crucial because:
- Child Benefit can be affected if a child is in care for more than 8 weeks
- Whether you're eligible can depend on if the local council was financially supporting the care arrangement

**What I recommend:**

You should contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances. They can:
- Help you determine whether the council was paying for Alex's care
- Clarify how this affects your entitlement to Child Benefit
- Advise you on whether you can claim or continue claiming now that Alex is back home with you

You can contact them by phone or post - the contact details are available through HMRC's Child Benefit service.
